name: KMS 'Enable IAM User Permissions' account-root delegation - broad account authority, NOT public, NOT root-user-only
note: IAM-1207 (properly-conditioned KMS negative control, suite-2 test 51). The standard KMS key-policy statement grants the account-root principal kms:* on Resource:* (the attached key). It delegates broad KMS authority to the OWNING ACCOUNT via IAM - it must NOT be classified as public access, must NOT be called root-user-only, and Resource:* must NOT explode into a per-key node.
rationale: The account-root ARN (arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root) delegates permissions to the whole account and its administrators - it is NOT the root user only, and it is NOT the public '*' principal, so neither a root-only claim nor PUBLIC-ACCESS is correct. The key is in the same account (111122223333), so this is not cross-account. In a KMS key policy, Resource:'*' means 'this KMS key' (the attached key), not every key in the account, so it must never be scored as an identity-style broad-resource wildcard (no WILDCARD-RESOURCE) and must never create a graph node per key. kms:* on the account principal enables the account to use IAM policies to delegate key access, so which individual principals are actually reachable is unknown without the account's identity policies. Ref: docs/resource-policy-semantics.md sec 6 / 7.1.
